instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63, and §13.63(1)(a) sets out the license application process — meaning lobbyist registration (licensing) is statutorily required.
Section 13.63(1)(a) provides that a lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, meaning the renewal cadence is biennial (every 24 months).

Lobbyists must obtain their own license under §13.63(1)(a), principals must file a separate registration statement under §13.64(1), and §13.65 requires a separate written authorization for each principal-lobbyist relationship, establishing separate registrations for lobbyists and their clients (principals).

Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the required contents of a lobbyist license application (signature, social security number, fee) and does not require submission of a photograph; no other section in the subchapter imposes a photo requirement.

Section 13.621(3) expressly exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency that files a statement under §13.695 (and its named officials) are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, creating a partial exemption for state agencies that file the §13.695 disclosure.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute does not specify a deadline in days for amending a lobbyist's license/registration; §13.64(3) requires principals to give written notice before lobbying in a new area but sets no numeric day-count, and §13.695(2) (10 days) applies only to agency statements, not lobbyists.

Wisconsin's statute requires the lobbyist to be licensed BEFORE engaging in lobbying (§13.66 and §13.65 require licensure/authorization before lobbying), and does not set a post-first-lobbying day deadline for the lobbyist's own registration; the 10-day trigger in §13.64(1) applies to principals exceeding $500, not to the lobbyist's licensing.
